best_for: Solo developers and small studios on Windows, macOS or Ubuntu who juggle Unity versions: one project on last year's Editor, another on the newest.
description:
Unity Hub is the free launcher from Unity Technologies for its Unity game engine. It is closed-source software, and you install it before the Unity Editor itself.

From the Hub you create new projects and open existing ones in the right Editor. You can browse templates, sample projects and learning material, and reach Unity Learn tutorials from the Learn icon in the toolbar. If you build several games the same way, you can save one of your own projects as a custom template and start the next one from it. The Hub also ships a copy of the Unity CLI, a command-line tool for installing Editors from scripts or build servers. Unity calls that tool experimental.

points.title: Several Editors side by side
points.text: Each project can stay on its own Editor version. The Hub installs those versions and their add-on modules, so you pick the one a project was built with instead of upgrading everything at once.

points.title: A Unity ID is required
points.text: Licences are activated by signing in with a Unity ID. On named-user plans an organisation admin assigns the seats, so you cannot activate one on your own. A licence activated by request cannot be returned from the Hub.

points.title: Free has conditions
points.text: Unity Personal is free for games and entertainment only, and for individuals or businesses under USD 200K of revenue or funding in the past 12 months. Above that, Pro is required; above USD 25M, Enterprise. Non-game apps from organisations over USD 1M need an Industry plan.

points.title: Console and Vision Pro builds
points.text: The pricing page lists console and Apple Vision Pro support under Pro, not Personal. Check this before planning a console port on the free tier.

points.title: Windows and macOS
points.text: Windows 10 (21H1 or later, 64-bit) and Windows 11 are supported, with a classic .exe installer and, since Hub 3.22, an MSIX package. macOS needs version 13 or later.

points.title: Linux is Ubuntu-first
points.text: The Linux install guide describes an apt repository run by Unity for Ubuntu, plus an AppImage that needs FUSE 3. RHEL, CentOS and Fedora are described as not officially supported. The Flatpak listed on this page is a separate route that the guide does not describe.

points.title: No Arm64 Linux Editor
points.text: The Editor does not support Linux on Arm64, so the Hub will not help you there even if it starts.
